text.en: Three short pieces take us to Goa, Coorg and Assam.

A Baker from Goa by Lucio Rodrigues recalls the Goan baker, called the pader, whose bread was part of every household, festival and wedding.
The baker came with his basket and a bamboo staff, and the children waited for his early morning visit. Bread-making is a living tradition from Portuguese times.
Coorg by Lokesh Abrol describes Kodagu in Karnataka, a land of mist, hills, rivers and coffee plantations.
The Kodavas are a brave, martial people and the Cauvery is their sacred river. Coorg is also known for its hospitality.
In Tea from Assam by Arup Kumar Datta, Rajvir travels by train with his classmate Pranjol to visit Pranjol's tea-garden home in Upper Assam.
They buy tea at a station and Rajvir says that people drink over eighty crore cups of tea every day.
The land turns green with miles of tea bushes. Pranjol says Assam has the largest concentration of plantations in the world.
The three pieces show the variety of Indian regions, foods and customs.

why.en: This shows how popular tea is.
